Subject: Aurora DPA - retention / onshore backup exceptions + evidence Qs

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks for taking another pass with us on retention and locality language. A few open items from our side after internal review of the redline (attached):

1) Backup window: we need clarity that short-lived onshore backups (for disaster recovery) may be retained for up to 45 days for EU-resident customers, with proof of deletion. Is Redwood comfortable with a 45-day max for onshore-only backups?

2) Certified erasure evidence: our security team requires a machine-readable manifest for each erase event (timestamp, object ids, logical scope). Can Redwood provide that level of proof or do you offer an attestation/certification alternative?

3) Logs: for troubleshooting, we may request up to 12 months of aggregated telemetry for joint incident analysis. Can you enumerate what telemetry is included and retention controls?

We attached annotated redlines and an example manifest format for reference. Hoping to align quickly so procurement can finish the routing.

Regards,
Samantha Park
Senior Counsel, Aurora.ai

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Park <samantha.park@aurora.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Aug 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora DPA - retention / onshore backup exceptions + evidence Qs

Samantha — thanks, good questions. Short answers up front, then an operational proposal below.

1) Onshore backup window: Redwood can support a business exception for EU-resident customers of up to 30 days for transient onshore backups; 45 days is operationally feasible but would require a contract-level justification and an elevated approval (we want to avoid extended windows across customers).

2) Certified erasure evidence: We can produce a machine-readable erasure manifest (JSON lines) from our deletion pipeline containing: timestamp, tenant id, object prefix, deletion job id, and the operator that triggered the job. For customers that require higher assurance, we offer a periodic signed attestation (quarterly) plus on-demand evidence exports for specific erasure jobs.

3) Logs: Our standard telemetry for incident analysis includes aggregated request counts, model identifiers, token-level metrics (aggregates only), and error traces. Raw user payloads are not retained beyond ephemeral KV caches unless explicitly stored for debugging (opt-in). We can commit to a 12-month aggregated telemetry retention with row-level pseudonymization.

Operational proposal (attached as a short playbook):
- Default: EU residency for production data and snapshots within EU regions.
- Exception: Onshore backups (for DR) limited to 30 days by default; 45 days possible with Business Justification Form + Legal sign-off.
- Evidence: Provide erasure manifest on demand within 5 business days. Quarterly signed attestation available as add-on.
- Logs: 12-month aggregate retention; request process for raw debug traces (business case + limited retention window).

I attached a short playbook table that maps redline clauses to operational controls and the artifacts we can provide. If that looks good, Laura and I can propose contract language tweaks that preserve the intent while keeping the operational guardrails.

-Markus
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Evidence_Playbook_Table.csv

Samantha / Markus —

From a legal drafting perspective, two pragmatic suggestions to make the DPA redline workable without opening broader precedent for all customers: 

- Add a clause: "Onshore Backup Exception: Limited to the specific customer request described in Annex B. Any extension beyond 30 days requires written Business Justification and explicit Legal approval." That keeps the default narrow and traceable.

- For erasure evidence, accept the machine-readable manifest approach in principle but include "attestation" language as an alternative where operational constraints make per-object manifests impractical. E.g., "Customer may request either (i) a per-erasure manifest produced by Provider, or (ii) a signed Provider attestation describing the scope and timing of the erasure."

I'll draft a suggested paragraph and share in-line redlines.

-Laura
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Aurora DPA - retention / onshore backup exceptions + evidence Qs

Quick ops note — implementing a 45-day onshore backup window impacts snapshot lifecycle and cross-region replication. If Aurora needs 45 days we can:

1) Tag the snapshots with a special exception tag and run a targeted retention job that expires only those objects after 45 days. This will increase S3 lifecycle policy complexity but is straightforward.
2) The manifest export will come from a daily deletion job; expect up to 24 hours for the manifest to be generated after job completion.
3) For the attestation alternative, we will need a standard template and a contact for sign-off.

We estimate 2 weeks of engineering time to add the exception-tagging flow and to include the manifest payload in the deletion pipeline. That can be delivered as a short SOW or as part of the Dedicated onboarding if you choose reserved capacity.

-Monica
Product Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Markus / Laura / Samantha —

Thanks for the clarity. Aurora's procurement asked us to formalize the requested clause and provide a DocuSign envelope that includes: the Annex B business justification form and the preferred erasure evidence option (manifest vs attestation).

Link to envelope: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/AUR-2247

We suggest the following redline (draft):
"Provider may maintain transient onshore backups for the Customer for up to forty-five (45) days for disaster recovery purposes solely where (i) Customer completes Annex B justifying the need, and (ii) Provider agrees in writing to the exception. Provider shall, upon Customer request, provide either (a) a machine-readable erasure manifest for any deletion job affecting Customer data, or (b) a signed attestation describing the scope and timing of the deletion. Evidence shall be provided within five (5) business days of request."

If Redwood can accept the language with the 45-day cap we can proceed to DocuSign. If Redwood prefers to keep the 30-day default with an approval path to 45, please indicate and we'll update the envelope.

Best,
BridgeCounsel LLP
